record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: What is the largest constant c such that every oriented graph has a vertex v satisfying |N++(v)| >= c |N+(v)|, where N++(v) is the second out-neighborhood and N+(v) is the out-neighborhood of v?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2 Find the largest coefficient c such that for any oriented graph, there is a vertex v satisfying the inequality |N ++(v)| ≥ c|N +(v)|.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An oriented graph is a directed graph with no loops and at most one directed edge between any two vertices (i.e., for any two distinct vertices u, v, at most one of the arcs (u,v) and (v,u) is present). For a vertex v in an oriented graph D, let N^+(v) denote the out-neighborhood of v, namely the set of vertices u such that (v,u) is an arc of D, and let N^{++}(v) denote the second out-neighborhood of v, namely the set of vertices w not in N^+(v) ∪ {v} such that there exists some u ∈ N^+(v) with (u,w) an arc of D.

Determine the largest real constant c with the following property: for every finite oriented graph D, there exists a vertex v of D such that
   |N^{++}(v)| ≥ c · |N^+(v)|.

(Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture asserts that c = 1 is attainable.)
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a weakening of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture (1990), which corresponds to c = 1. The conjecture remains open in general; it is verified for tournaments (Fisher) and various subclasses (quasi-transitive, random/pseudorandom orientations, small orders, m-free digraphs), and partial bounds on c (such as the Chen–Shen–Yuster constant ≈ 0.6573 for tournaments and λ_m-type bounds for m-free oriented graphs) are known, but the exact largest constant for all oriented graphs has not been determined.

status_evidence.title: Second neighborhood problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Seymour conjectured that in every oriented graph there exists a vertex whose second neighborhood is at least as large as its first neighborhood.
status_evidence.claim: Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture (c=1) is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Seymour's second neighbourhood conjecture: random graphs and reductions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work (2024-2025) continues to attack the conjecture for random graphs and via reductions, indicating the problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on the conjecture supports its open status.

status_evidence.title: Seymour's Second Neighbourhood Conjecture for Oriented Graphs of Order at Most Seven
status_evidence.snippet: Verifies the conjecture for small orders, indicating it is not resolved in general.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is verified only for restricted classes.
